dossier.summary: The project supports a conditional bias–variance account of regression GATE error, sharp curvature sensitivity bounds, and contrasting symmetry and unsupported-exposure cases. Fixed-graph simulations show that a correctly specified cubic regression can have much worse endpoint error than a linear fit, while matched deletion controls support the role of low-degree observations. The code, generated summaries, and recorded simulation and reproduction runs support the main empirical comparisons, with the scope limited to the stated synthetic response laws and known covariance. The selected prediction score reuses its selection data, a limitation explicitly disclosed in the figure caption; the endpoint-error evaluation does not select on endpoint truth. Raw per-repetition files and the graph were excluded from this review copy by the manifest, limiting independent reconstruction, and the printed paper retains a template error.

claims.quote: On fixed synthetic networks and the public ego-Facebook graph, repeated CPU simulations show that correctly specifying a cubic response can greatly increase GATE error: on degree-128 regular graphs its RMSE is \RCHigh{}, versus \RLHigh{} for a misspecified linear fit.
scope_words: On fixed synthetic networks and the public ego-Facebook graph

claims.quote: We express its conditional error through endpoint weights and derive a sharp, computable worst-case bias bound under a common exposure-response curvature constraint.
scope_words: under a common exposure-response curvature constraint

a coupling argument demonstrates failure when high-exposure responses are almost never observed.

neither ordinary predictive accuracy nor model correctness alone certifies accurate GATE estimation.

issues.quote: The selected validation score is a minimum and is optimistically biased as a risk estimate.
issues.why: Figure 3 reports the held-out MSE minimized to choose CV-select, so that curve is not an independent estimate of selected-model prediction risk. The caption explicitly concedes this, and the separately computed GATE error still supports the endpoint-versus-prediction distinction.

evaluation_errors.why: The prediction MSE reported for CV-select is the same minimum held-out score used at line 219 to select the polynomial. It is optimistic as prediction-risk evaluation; Figure 3 explicitly labels this limitation, and selection does not use true endpoint error.

process_notes: Counts classify command entries, not individual simulation cells. One experiment command contains both validation and saturation; the full reproduction command reruns all suites. Mixed analysis/build commands are classified as figure when their analysis generates figures and summaries.

Rework counts the support-ablation rerun after the first paper draft and the full reproduction run. Repeated rendering, table regeneration and PDF builds are excluded from this experimental-rework count.

Four failure entries are marked recovered in tables.json. The failed source download was followed by a documented decision not to cite it as consulted; the final missing-directory and archive-API problems were retried. A search returning no warning matches and a git-status check outside a repository do not show failed experiments.

Some trajectory command outputs and edit diffs explicitly carry truncation metadata. Integrity findings are confined to the visible commands, outputs, final code and disclosed changes; omitted text is not counted as missing work.
The compressed raw simulation files and public graph were excluded by MANIFEST.json, while summaries, run metadata, numerical generation code and comparison logs remain available.

integrity.why: The implemented CV-select polynomial is chosen by held-out noisy-outcome MSE, and that same minimized MSE is plotted as its prediction score in Figure 3 (study.py lines 207, 219–221; analyze.py lines 179–180). The caption explicitly calls the score optimistic. This finding concerns the prediction-score panel only: endpoint truth is not used for selection, and the separately reported GATE error evaluates the resulting selection procedure.

The inspected history adds curvature/threshold diagnostics, adds an equal-count random-deletion control after inspecting the first ablation, and later adds Wilson coverage intervals. These changes are disclosed in main.tex lines 173, 370 and 380; the original degree-cutoff results are retained. No inspected change silently favors a reported evaluation result.

The simulation generates outcomes, trains candidates on the training-node subset, and uses the permitted held-out subset for the stated prediction-selection procedure. Fixed regression weights depend on treatment/exposure features rather than true endpoint effects; true means and GATE enter diagnostics after estimation. No forbidden evaluation-label access is shown.

All numerical source artifacts map to recorded simulation or analysis commands, and a full reproduction plus numerical comparison is recorded. The manifest's omitted compressed raw files limit this review's reconstruction but are not evidence of an absent run.
